title: Is modified citrus pectin an effective heavy metal binder?

grade.title: Small, uncontrolled, or single-source human evidence
grade.basis: One uncontrolled pilot. The lead result was not statistically significant at p<0.05.

answerHtml: An uncontrolled 6-day pilot reported higher 24-hour urinary arsenic, cadmium, and lead after modified citrus pectin. Arsenic rose 130 percent on day 1 and cadmium 150 percent on day 6. The lead increase was 560 percent with p<0.08, which is above a conventional 0.05 cutoff. The sample size was not stated in the abstract, so it is not given here. There is no control group and no clinical outcome.

sections.heading: Study
sections.html: Eliaz and colleagues (2006), PMID 16835878, doi:10.1002/ptr.1953. The lead author was affiliated with a clinic, and the abstract names a product. PubMed.
